document_control.title: STRUCTURED_BLANK_PAGE_INTAKE_PHASE_1_CLASSIFICATION_REVIEW_PACKET_V1
document_control.primary_objective: Establish the exact human review, adjudication, calibration, and release-gating protocol for Phase 1 intake classification in machine-readable form so the system can be tested, corrected, and trusted before broader rollout.

purpose.description: Phase 1 of Structured Blank Page Intake is a decision surface that converts messy student inputs into a stable, reviewable classification state trusted by downstream systems.
failure_risks: loss of student trust at the first meaningful interaction
questions_this_packet_must_answer: What exactly is the classifier being judged on?
How should humans label difficult or ambiguous cases?
How do we distinguish acceptable uncertainty from system weakness?
What error patterns are tolerable in Phase 1 and which are release blockers?
What evidence is required before this layer is allowed to ship?

relationships.conflict_rule: If any rule in this packet conflicts with a frozen upstream architecture or release-quality artifact, the conflict must be resolved explicitly and versioned. Silent drift is prohibited.

must_demonstrate: identify the correct intake state or mode from user-provided inputs
extract and classify the correct signal family profile from a structured blank page interaction
distinguish between clear, weak, ambiguous, and insufficient-evidence cases
avoid overclaiming confidence where evidence is thin
produce deterministic, reviewable outputs under equivalent inputs
expose failure patterns in a way that can be corrected systematically
review_objective.success_standard: The intake classifier behaves like a disciplined, uncertainty-aware system rather than a persuasive but unstable AI layer.

classification_unit_under_review.review_target: Classification behavior mapping structured blank page intake inputs into a normalized Phase 1 interpretation object.

core_review_principles.name: truth_over_fluency
core_review_principles.rule: A terse correct classification is better than a fluent but wrong interpretation.

core_review_principles.name: evidence_over_intuition
core_review_principles.rule: Labels must be assigned based on observable evidence in the case, not reviewer projection or what the student probably meant.

core_review_principles.name: uncertainty_must_be_explicit
core_review_principles.rule: Where evidence is mixed, thin, contradictory, or low-signal, the correct behavior is to surface ambiguity or insufficiency, not to force precision.

core_review_principles.name: determinism_matters
core_review_principles.rule: Equivalent inputs should yield materially equivalent classification outputs. Variation that changes routing or mode assignment without evidence change is a defect.

core_review_principles.name: reviewability_is_mandatory
core_review_principles.rule: Every judged case must be auditable by another reviewer after the fact.

core_review_principles.name: error_asymmetry_matters
core_review_principles.rule: Errors that misdirect the student early, create false certainty, or corrupt downstream narrative work are prioritized as more severe.

packet_deliverables.name: packet_index
packet_deliverables.requirement: Top-level index listing all included materials, version numbers, owners, and last-updated timestamps.

packet_deliverables.name: label_schema_reference
packet_deliverables.requirement: Authoritative reference for primary intake modes, allowed secondary tags, signal families, ambiguity classes, insufficiency classes, contradiction classes, and escalation triggers aligned with implementation and labeling specs.

packet_deliverables.name: gold_set_case_pack
packet_deliverables.requirement: Curated set representing the real decision surface, including easy, medium, hard, ambiguous, insufficient-evidence, contradictory, deceptive/low-effort, and route-breaking edge cases.

packet_deliverables.name: adjudication_notes
packet_deliverables.requirement: Per-gold-case record of final label, winning rationale, alternatives considered, alternatives rejected, and taxonomy weakness exposure.

packet_deliverables.name: calibration_set
packet_deliverables.requirement: Reviewer calibration subset used before broader evaluation begins.

packet_deliverables.name: blind_evaluation_set
packet_deliverables.requirement: Held-out set for actual measurement not repeatedly tuned against by reviewers or prompt engineers.

packet_deliverables.name: error_taxonomy
packet_deliverables.requirement: Normalized taxonomy of model failure patterns.

packet_deliverables.name: scoring_and_acceptance_sheet
packet_deliverables.requirement: Standardized scoring template for per-case judgment and release readiness.

packet_deliverables.name: change_log
packet_deliverables.requirement: Every meaningful packet change must be versioned, dated, and reason-coded.

primary_mode_label.rule: Reflect the dominant actionable state of the student input, not merely the most emotionally salient phrase.

secondary_tag_set.rule: Capture meaningful but non-dominant attributes that affect routing or interpretation.
secondary_tag_set.prohibition: Must not be used as a crutch for avoiding a hard primary classification decision.

signal_family_profile.rule: Evaluate whether the classifier correctly detects the relevant Phase 1 signal families.

ambiguity_status.rule: Reward correct identification of genuinely ambiguous cases.

insufficiency_status.rule: Reward correct identification of cases with inadequate evidence rather than fabricated structure.

review_or_escalation_flag.rule: Judge whether the flag was correctly raised when the defined threshold for human intervention was met.

gold_set_construction_rules.purpose: Truth anchor benchmark capturing the actual operating environment.
gold_set_construction_rules.small_set_rule: Smaller sets may be used temporarily, but release decisions based on extremely small sets are provisional.
gold_set_construction_rules.anti_contamination_rule: Cases used for major prompt iteration should not be over-recycled as the sole evidence of success. Hold-out data is mandatory.

case_format_standard.input_payload_rule: Preserve the exact text and structured selections relevant to classification. Reviewers should never label from a paraphrase when the original is available.

difficulty_bands.A: Clear: dominant signal is obvious, low ambiguity.
difficulty_bands.B: Moderate: one likely answer, but non-trivial competing interpretations exist.
difficulty_bands.C: Hard: requires close reading and disciplined taxonomy application.
difficulty_bands.D: Ambiguous: multiple interpretations remain materially plausible even after close reading.
difficulty_bands.E: Insufficient: evidence too weak to support a trustworthy primary interpretation.

adjudication_protocol.why_necessary: Raw reviewer disagreement is diagnostic information and must be used to determine whether the issue lies in the model, taxonomy, instructions, case, or reviewer inconsistency.
adjudication_protocol.decision_standard: The winning label is the one best supported by actual evidence and frozen label definitions, not seniority.
adjudication_protocol.taxonomy_change_rule: Changes should be rare and justified only when repeated cases reveal a structural mismatch between reality and the current label framework.

reviewer_instructions.job_definition: Classify the intake artifact in front of you using the allowed taxonomy and evidence only.
review_sequence: Determine whether the evidence supports a single dominant primary mode.
Assign secondary tags only if independently justified.
Mark escalation if the defined trigger is met.

acceptable_style: explains why ambiguity is or is not warranted

errors.name: wrong_primary_mode
errors.definition: The dominant mode assignment is incorrect and would materially alter routing or downstream interpretation.

errors.name: missing_dominant_signal
errors.definition: The model failed to detect the strongest relevant signal family present in the case.

errors.name: false_dominant_signal
errors.definition: The model elevated a weak or absent signal into a decisive classification factor.

errors.name: overconfidence_under_ambiguity
errors.definition: The case should have been marked ambiguous or low-confidence, but the system presented a decisive answer.

errors.name: false_ambiguity
errors.definition: The case was sufficiently clear, but the system avoided a valid decision by over-flagging ambiguity.

errors.name: failure_to_detect_insufficiency
errors.definition: The input lacked enough evidence, but the system fabricated structure or certainty.

errors.name: false_insufficiency
errors.definition: The case contained enough evidence for a stable call, but the system incorrectly labeled it as insufficient.

errors.name: contradiction_handling_failure
errors.definition: The system failed to detect or properly respond to materially contradictory inputs.

errors.name: secondary_tag_distortion
errors.definition: Secondary labels were wrong in a way that meaningfully changes interpretation or route behavior.

errors.name: escalation_failure
errors.definition: The system missed a case that required review or unnecessarily escalated a normal case.

errors.name: non_deterministic_output_drift
errors.definition: Equivalent or near-equivalent inputs produced materially different classifications without justified cause.

errors.name: rationale_or_observability_defect
errors.definition: The system output could not be meaningfully reviewed because rationale or structured explanation was inadequate, inconsistent, or missing.

severity_bands.name: critical
severity_bands.definition: Release blocker; materially misroutes or misleads the student.

severity_bands.name: major
severity_bands.definition: Serious quality issue; weakens trust or downstream quality.

severity_bands.name: minor
severity_bands.definition: Low-risk issue; does not materially change route or interpretation.

error_taxonomy.repeated_pattern_escalation_rule: A single S2 error may be tolerable depending on frequency. Repeated S2 patterns across the same slice are a gating concern.

scoring_framework.purpose: Support release judgment without creating a false impression of mathematical precision.
scoring_framework.critical_axis_rule: A case may not receive an overall pass if a critical axis fails in a way that would materially harm routing.

acceptance_and_release_thresholds.minimum_qualitative_standard: The classifier behaves like a disciplined educational product layer that knows when it knows, knows when it does not know, and can be corrected by humans without forensic guesswork.
acceptance_and_release_thresholds.threshold_rule: These are starting thresholds. If actual user risk suggests a stricter bar, the stricter bar wins.

calibration_protocol.purpose: Ensure reviewers are applying the taxonomy consistently before evaluation results are trusted.
process: Reviewers independently label the calibration subset.
Instructions are refined only if necessary.
A second pass is run if the first pass reveals major inconsistency.
calibration_protocol.success_standard: Calibration is sufficient when disagreements are explainable, bounded, and not driven by basic taxonomy confusion.
calibration_protocol.pause_condition: If reviewers cannot reliably separate resolvable cases from ambiguous or insufficient cases, evaluation should pause until the framework is corrected.

determinism_and_stability_checks.failure_rule: If minor perturbations materially change routing or dominant classification without real semantic change, log an E11 defect.

human_review_escalation_rules.usage_rule: Human review should be used to preserve trust and learning quality, not as a blanket crutch for weak system design.

packet_governance.versioning_rule: Every material change to labels, adjudication logic, scoring rules, thresholds, blind-set composition, or reviewer instructions must increment the packet version or recorded revision stamp.
packet_governance.freeze_discipline: Do not change packet rules mid-evaluation unless the run is explicitly invalidated and restarted.
